Extract latent positions as a tidy data frame

Source: R/latent_positions.R
latent_positions.Rd

Extracts multiplicative latent factor positions (U and V) from a fitted ame, lame or ame_als model and returns them as a tidy data frame suitable for plotting and analysis, with posterior standard deviations when posterior draws of the positions are available.

Usage

latent_positions(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ame'
latent_positions(object, align = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lame'
latent_positions(object, align = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ame_als'
latent_positions(object, align = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted ame, lame or ame_als model object with R > 0.

...

Additional arguments (currently unused).

align

Logical. For dynamic ame_als fits, apply Procrustes alignment across the time periods of the fit. It has no effect on ame fits (a single period) or on lame fits, whose dynamic positions are aligned when the model is fitted (see Details).

Value

A data frame with columns:

actor

Character. Actor name (from rownames of U or V).

dimension

Integer. Latent dimension index (1 to R).

time

Character. Time period label. Dynamic fits use the time labels from the input; static (cross-sectional) fits return "1" for every row so downstream filtering by time behaves the same in both cases.

value

Numeric. The posterior mean latent position.

posterior_sd

Numeric. Posterior standard deviation of the latent position, or NA if posterior draws are not available. To enable, fit the model with posterior_opts = posterior_options(save_UV = TRUE) (static positions) or posterior_opts = list(save_UV_draws = TRUE) (dynamic positions). An ame_als fit, or a lame(method = "als") fit with static factors, reports the sd of each reported coordinate under its Laplace posterior (fit$U_sd, fit$V_sd), with the directions that leave the product unchanged left out.

type

Character. "U" for sender/row positions, "V" for receiver/column positions. Symmetric models have only "U".

Returns a zero-row data frame with correct column names if R = 0.

For a fit with static positions (ame, lame without dynamic_uv, and static ame_als fits) the data frame carries an attribute "strength": a data frame with one row per dimension and columns dimension, strength (the singular value of the reported product for that dimension, or the absolute eigenvalue for symmetric fits), share (its squared strength over the sum of the squared strengths) and tied_with_next. Dimensions \(j\) and \(j + 1\) are tied when the reported gap between their strengths is less than twice the posterior sd of that gap over the saved draws (each draw's own strengths): the two axes are then not well separated and are read together as a plane, and a message says so. tied_with_next is NA for fits without saved draws of the positions. Fits with dynamic_uv = TRUE carry no strength attribute: their per-period positions are rotated to match the period before, so a column is not one dimension of each period's product.

Details

The latent product of each period is identified, the positions only up to a rotation or sign change that leaves the product unchanged. The positions of a static ame or lame fit therefore factor the posterior mean product at the fitted rank, with columns in decreasing order of its singular values and the sign of each column set so that its positive entries carry more of its squared length than its negative ones: \(U V'\) with the scale split evenly between \(U\) and \(V\); \(U L U'\) for symmetric fits, with \(U\) orthonormal and fit$L the eigenvalues largest in absolute value; and \(U G V'\) for bipartite fits, with the scale split evenly and fit$G the identity (when R_row and R_col differ, the product has rank \(k\), the smaller of the two, the columns of fit$U or fit$V past \(k\) are zero, and only the \(k\) dimensions are listed). The positions of a lame fit with dynamic_uv = TRUE factor the posterior mean product of every period at the fitted rank: \(U_t V_t'\) with the scale split evenly between \(U_t\) and \(V_t\); \(U_t L U_t'\) for symmetric fits, with fit$L fixed across periods; and \(U_t G V_t'\) for bipartite fits, with a diagonal fit$G fixed across periods. Each period is matched to the one before by moves that keep its product. The posterior standard deviations come from the saved draws (posterior_opts = posterior_options(save_UV = TRUE) for static positions, posterior_opts = list(save_UV_draws = TRUE) for dynamic ones), each draw factored the same way and matched onto the reported positions by a move that leaves its product unchanged (a rotation, or a relabelling and sign change of the columns when L or a dynamic G is held fixed).

Alignment only ever happens across the periods of one fit. Nothing here aligns two different fits (two chains, or the same model with and without a covariate) to a common orientation, so their latent positions are not directly comparable. To compare fits that way, stack their U matrices into an [n, R, 2] array (same actors in the same order, same R) and call procrustes_align(U = that_array) on it.

See also

procrustes_align for standalone Procrustes alignment, uv_plot for visualizing latent positions, posterior_options for enabling posterior sampling of U/V

Author

Cassy Dorff, Shahryar Minhas, Tosin Salau

Examples

# \donttest{
data(YX_nrm)
# chains = 1 keeps the example short; the default runs two chains and compares them
fit <- ame(YX_nrm$Y, Xdyad = YX_nrm$X, R = 2,
           burn = 5, nscan = 5, odens = 1, verbose = FALSE, chains = 1)
lp <- latent_positions(fit)
head(lp)
#>   actor dimension time      value posterior_sd type
#> 1 node1         1    1  0.1820285   0.06411356    U
#> 2 node2         1    1 -0.6502813   0.12446819    U
#> 3 node3         1    1 -0.1695219   0.13456369    U
#> 4 node4         1    1  0.2035775   0.10322440    U
#> 5 node5         1    1 -0.2482276   0.07926787    U
#> 6 node6         1    1 -0.1786310   0.07715069    U
# }
